newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish police foil guerrilla rocket attack.
newsitem.headline: Irish police foil guerrilla rocket attack.

text.p: Irish security sources said on Monday they believed they had foiled an attack on British troops in Northern Ireland after seizing armaments at a suspected guerrilla training camp in the republic.
Police said they had found a primed rocket warhead containing around 600 grammes of what appeared to be Semtex, a commercial high explosive often used by IRA guerrillas.
"There was an armed device known as a PRIG (propelled rocket improvised grenade) along with a launcher. It was ready for use," police superintendent Kevin Lennon told Reuters.
"We hope that we saved lives, that is our primary objective."
Police also seized two Kalashnikov AK 47 assault rifles, ammunition, training manuals and other "explosives material" when they raided a shed in remote farmland in Donegal, Ireland.
Six men were arrested and one was later released. The remaining suspects, all from Northern Ireland, are being questioned under Ireland's counter-insurgency laws.
The area of the raid is some 20 miles (30 kms) from the border with Northern Ireland.
It was the latest in a series of successes by Irish security forces who have unearthed caches of mortars and arms hidden by the banned Irish Republican Army.
Security has been tightened in Northern Ireland since an IRA bomb attack at British army headquarters in Lisburn, south of Belfast, three weeks ago which killed a soldier.
It was the first time the guerrillas had struck in the province since abandoning a 17-month truce in February.LONDON,
